en.text: Acacia bivenosa, commonly known as two-nerved wattle, two-veined wattle, hill umbrella bush, dune wattle or Cable Beach wattle is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to northern Australia. It is a bushy, rounded or spreading shrub with narrowly elliptic, oblong or egg-shaped to lance-shaped phyllodes, rich golden-yellow flowers in spherical heads, and erect, crust-like to more or less woody pods up to 80 mm (3.1 in) long.

pt.text: Acacia bivenosa é uma espécie de leguminosa do gênero Acacia, pertencente à família Fabaceae.

id.text: Acacia bivenosa merupakan anggota famili Fabaceae yang tersebar luas di wilayah utara Australia dan dikenal sebagai semak padat dengan bentuk yang membulat atau melebar. Filodanya bervariasi, mulai dari elips sempit, lonjong, hingga menyerupai telur atau tombak, sementara bunganya tersusun dalam kepala bulat berwarna kuning keemasan yang kaya. Polongnya tegak, bertekstur keras hingga semi-kayu, dan dapat tumbuh hingga sekitar 80 mm panjangnya.

en.heading: Uses
en.text: The bush can be heavily grazed by stock, especially as a seedling. Indigenous Australians used to find edible grubs from around the roots. It is often used in land rehabilitation as a primary colonizer.
